rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=6, train_n=200, n_iter=300, val_n=16, grad_clip=2.0, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, outer_wall_s=1500, seed=42, rationale=iter-11 CEILING-CONFIRMATION PROBE: ONE knob grad_clip 1.0->2.0 (LOOSER per-scan Adam gradient clip) on the iter-4 ep6 PEAK cfg (ep6, lr=1e-4, c16, n_iter300, val_n16, seed42 -> 0.9596). This is the genuinely-untried direction on the grad_clip axis: iter-8 tested the TIGHTER 0.5 (0.9597, flat), iter-9 reset to the mandatory 1.0 floor; 2.0 (looser) has never been tried and tests whether the per-scan trajectory was being OVER-clipped at the 1.0 floor. NOT-yet-tried axis = looser-than-mandatory per-scan grad-clip strength; it perturbs only the per-scan optimization-trajectory stability, no read knob (val_n/seed fixed), so the comparison to the 0.9596 ep6 peak stays apples-to-apples. EXHAUSTED axes AVOIDED: lr anchored 1e-4 (iter-3 0.9553->0.9593); n_iter HURTS via per-scan overfit, no early-stop (iter-2 n_iter600 0.9553->0.9407); pretrain_epochs ep6 PEAK (ep3->6 up 0.9593->0.9596, ep9 DOWN 0.9593 iter-10, ep12 down 0.9585 iter-5); unet_c flat (iter-6 c16->c32 0.9596->0.9495); seed noise-stable (iter-7 seed123 0.9588); grad_clip TIGHTER 0.5 flat (iter-8 0.9597); val_n a read knob not a lever (iter-9 val_n24 0.9609 = cleaner read of the same recon); warm_start LOAD-BEARING-POSITIVE, kept True NEVER off. Failure mode: per-image U-Net N2I on dense-view 128-angle breast is STRUCTURALLY FBP-BOUNDED -- the half-angle view-split discards information the full-view 128-view LD-FBP keeps, so each per-scan GT-free fit caps BELOW the LD-FBP baseline (hr=0); a substrate ceiling, not an optimization/capacity one. Hypothesis: 0.9596 is a substrate FBP-bound ceiling, so a looser grad_clip=2.0 lands WITHIN NOISE of the ep6 peak (hr stays 0), documenting that the ~0.96 breast per-image U-Net N2I ceiling is grad-clip-DIRECTION-insensitive (insensitive to both tightening to 0.5 AND loosening to 2.0) and structurally FBP-bounded, toward the iter-20 ceiling-documentation mandate. A material LIFT would mean the per-scan trajectory was being over-clipped at the 1.0 floor (a real capacity-to-climb lever after all); a material drop would mean the per-scan FBP-adjoint needs the tighter 1.0 clip to stay stable. Wall: iter-4 (ep6, gc1.0, val_n16) ran 468s; identical cfg except the grad_clip threshold value changes nothing about FLOPs/iters -> est ~470-500s, well under the 900s/15-min wall (outer_wall_s=1500 hard cap).
